verdicts.photo_observation: Cable-routing photos (pages 12-19) show all AC/DC/earthing cable paths running along parapet walls, building exterior surfaces, and through a drilled wall hole (page 16, captioned 'Make a hole to run the DC cable up to the inverter location') rather than through any underground trench; no dug-up ground or trench work appears anywhere in the documentation.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Following the Cable Routing Legend (page 4) colors across pages 12-19: the red/green (DC + DC-earthing) lines start at the rooftop PV area (page 12), continue along the parapet and down the building face (pages 13-16, with an explicit 'make a hole to run the DC cable up to the inverter location' callout on page 16) to the Inverter/ACDB/DCDB and Battery markers in the equipment room (page 17). The purple AC-cable line runs from the ACDB/DCDB box to the main distribution panel and is captioned 'The output AC cable has to be terminated near the main power supply' (page 18), continuing to the new Solar Meter slot beside the Main Meter (page 19). The green earthing lines and orange LA line run down a separate building face route (pages 15-16) to dedicated AC Earth Pit, DC Earth Pit and LA Pit markers in the side corridor (page 19). No dangling or orphan line ends were observed across this run.
verdicts.rationale: The color-coded routing is traceable end-to-end with matching captions bridging every hop, though it is the design team's proposed/annotated overlay on photos rather than a physically completed installation photographed in situ.
